newsitem.title: USA: Westell has confidence in Internet link.
newsitem.headline: Westell has confidence in Internet link.

text.p: Westell Technologies Inc said Friday that although it has yet to confirm customer orders for the next version of its Internet connection products, it still believes the technology will be a financial success.

"Nothing firm," Stephen Hawrysz, chief financial officer for the telecommunications technology company, said in an interview. "But the indications are that this is a market which is going to be robust...I don't think that it is unusual in this business to not have a long backlog of orders."
Earlier Friday, Westell warned that results for its fiscal third quarter ending December 31 would not meet expectations.

Hawrysz said its FlexCap Rate Adaptive Digital Subscriber Line (RADSL) system is now expected to be launched in January. The company had previously said it would release it by the end of 1996. The technology allows for very high-speed connection to the Internet via traditional telephone lines.

However, the product launch delay has prompted customers to put off purchasing Westell's current product in anticipation of the faster, cheaper RADSL. As a result, Westell is considering taking a $0.07 to $0.09 a share charge to dispose of inventories.
"We had early indications that there would be more demand for our 1.5 (megabits per second) platform," Hawrysz said of the current digital subscriber line technology.
"RADSL is right around the corner and people realize that really has significant benefits," he added.
Security analysts had pegged fiscal third quarter revenues from the digital subscriber line technology alone at $15 million to $17 million. Westell said Friday it will not meet those expectations.
In fact, the company said it expects total revenues for the quarter in the $17 million range.
Westell's shares fell on the disappointing earnings projection, off 4-3/8 to 23-5/8 on turnover of more than four million shares.
Cowen & Co downgraded its rating on the stock to neutral from buy.

Kevin Slocum, an analyst for Soundview Financial Group, said he now expects third quarter revenues for the digital subscriber line technology of about $1.5 million. But he is also betting the technology is going to take off.
"I think we're going to see some interesting announcements from carriers that are committed to the technology over the next 30 to 60 days," said Slocum.
Slocum continues to rate the stock a buy, adding, "I'm unshaken, others are."

Westell did say it expects revenues in fiscal fourth quarter to top the third quarter's, enabling it to post a corresponding reduction in net losses. But Hawrysz declined to project beyond the fourth quarter.
"I'm not prepared to comment on fiscal '98," Hawrysz said.
